skill.name: browsing-with-playwright
skill.description: Use a local Playwright MCP server to navigate pages, click elements, fill forms, take screenshots, and extract page data. Best for browser automation, UI checks, and approved web research tasks.
skill.summary: Automate approved browser workflows through a local Playwright MCP server.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: The skill is a functional Playwright MCP browser automation package with expected network and local command use. Most Markdown backtick and JSON Schema URL detections are false positives, but the stdio transport runs arbitrary shell commands and helper scripts manage external processes. The package should be published only with clear warnings and hardening for command execution, package pinning, and PID-file handling.

remediation.issue: Stdio transport executes an arbitrary command with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Remove shell=True and require an argv list, or restrict stdio commands to a reviewed allowlist.

remediation.issue: The start script runs @playwright/mcp@latest through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the package version and document the expected package integrity or installation process.

remediation.issue: Server lifecycle scripts use predictable PID files in /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Use a private runtime directory, validate PID file ownership, and reject non-numeric PID values.

remediation.issue: Documentation encourages powerful browser actions on live pages.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance to avoid unauthorized sites, real credentials, payments, and destructive form submissions.

content.value_statement: Browser tasks need stateful clicks, forms, screenshots, and extraction. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a local Playwright MCP workflow.
actual_capabilities: Starts and stops a local Playwright MCP server with provided shell scripts.
Calls MCP browser tools through HTTP JSON-RPC using mcp-client.py.
Navigates pages, captures accessibility snapshots, and saves screenshots.
Clicks, types, fills forms, selects options, and waits for page state.
Documents browser_evaluate and browser_run_code for advanced Playwright actions.
limitations: Requires Node.js, npx, Python 3, and Playwright browser dependencies.
Uses local command execution and network access; review commands before running.
Browser actions can change live websites or submit real forms.
Does not provide credential management, captcha solving, or authorization bypass.

use_cases.title: Check Web Application Flows
use_cases.description: Run repeatable browser steps, capture page state, and collect screenshots for UI verification.

use_cases.title: Collect Approved Page Data
use_cases.description: Navigate permitted websites and extract visible content through snapshots or browser evaluation.

use_cases.title: Debug Interactive Forms
use_cases.description: Inspect form fields, test clicks and typing, and verify submission behavior in a real browser.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the Playwright MCP server, open this approved URL, and describe the visible page state.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to this page, capture an accessibility snapshot, take a full-page screenshot, and summarize important findings.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the browser snapshot to find the form fields, fill test values, submit the form, and report the result.

prompt_templates.title: Run Multi-Step Browser Logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright MCP to perform this approved multi-step browser task, verify each state change, and capture final evidence.

output_examples.input: Open a product page and capture what is visible.
output_examples.output: The browser opened the page, captured a snapshot, saved a screenshot, and summarized title, price, and visible status.

output_examples.input: Test a contact form with sample data.
output_examples.output: The form fields were located, sample values were entered, the submit action completed, and the confirmation message was reported.

output_examples.input: Extract table rows from an approved dashboard.
output_examples.output: The visible table content was collected, key rows were summarized, and the browser session was closed.

best_practices: Use the skill only on websites where browser automation is allowed.
Review commands before starting the MCP server or closing processes.
Stop the server when the browser task is complete.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to bypass authentication, paywalls, rate limits, or captcha controls.
Do not submit real credentials or payments through automated forms.
Do not browse untrusted sites with sensitive browser sessions active.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates browser navigation, page inspection, screenshots, clicks, typing, form filling, and selected Playwright actions.

faq.question: Does it need a local server?
faq.answer: Yes. The included scripts start a local Playwright MCP server before browser commands are sent.

faq.question: Can it access external websites?
faq.answer: Yes. Browser navigation can load external sites, so users should only target approved pages.

faq.question: Can it run JavaScript in the browser?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented evaluate and run-code tools can execute browser-side Playwright logic.

faq.question: Is it safe for production credentials?
faq.answer: No. Avoid real secrets, payment data, or privileged sessions unless your environment is approved.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
